messages.subject: Summary Fit Display on CFA
parts:
Greetings all. I'm trying to run a CFA using Lavaan with a large N = 1639. My code is below (apologies about the long variable names!).

#Baseline Model for 10-factor ASQ Instrument Using CFA Maximum Likelihood

baseline.model <- 'HL =~ Q10_HOMELIFE_1 + Q10_HOMELIFE_2 + Q10_HOMELIFE_3 + Q10_HOMELIFE_4 + Q10_HOMELIFE_5 + Q10_HOMELIFE_6 + Q10_HOMELIFE_7 + Q10_HOMELIFE_8 + Q10_HOMELIFE_9 + Q10_HOMELIFE_10 + Q10_HOMELIFE_11 + Q10_HOMELIFE_12
SP =~ Q10_SCHOOLPERF_1 + Q10_SCHOOLPERF_2 + Q10_SCHOOLPERF_3 + Q10_SCHOOLPERF_4 + Q10_SCHOOLPERF_5 + Q10_SCHOOLPERF_6 + Q10_SCHOOLPERF_7
SA =~ Q10_SCHOOLATTEND_1 + Q10_SCHOOLATTEND_2 + Q10_SCHOOLATTEND_3
RR =~ Q10_ROMANTIC_1 + Q10_ROMANTIC_2 + Q10_ROMANTIC_3 + Q10_ROMANTIC_4 + Q10_ROMANTIC_5
PP =~ Q11_PEERPRES_1 + Q11_PEERPRES_2 + Q11_PEERPRES_3 + Q11_PEERPRES_4 + Q11_PEERPRES_5 + Q11_PEERPRES_6 + Q11_PEERPRES_7
TI =~ Q11_TEACHER_1 + Q11_TEACHER_2 + Q11_TEACHER_3 + Q11_TEACHER_4 + Q11_TEACHER_5 + Q11_TEACHER_6 + Q11_TEACHER_7
FU =~ Q11_FUTUREUNC_1 + Q11_FUTUREUNC_2 + Q11_FUTUREUNC_3
SL =~ Q11_SCHOOLLEISURECONF_1 + Q11_SCHOOLLEISURECONF_2 + Q11_SCHOOLLEISURECONF_3 + Q11_SCHOOLLEISURECONF_4 + Q11_SCHOOLLEISURECONF_5
FP =~ Q11_FINANCIAL_1 + Q11_FINANCIAL_2 + Q11_FINANCIAL_3 + Q11_FINANCIAL_4
AR =~ Q11_ADULTRESP_1 + Q11_ADULTRESP_2 + Q11_ADULTRESP_3'

fit <- lavaan::cfa(model = baseline.model, data=ASQforLavaan)
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)

---
Everything seems to compute correctly until I ask for the summary function, which simply tells me the following. Any suggestions or advice? Thanks in advance. Valerie

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Summary Fit Display on CFA
parts:
Valerie,
  The other packages are not disabling the cfa() function but merely masking it.  To see how that works, try the following.

F # R returns FALSE
F <- TRUE # Masks the native F with a user assigned object of the same name
F # R returns TRUE
rm(F) # unmask the native F by deleting the user defined F
F # R returns FALSE again.

  So, the lavaan cfa() function is always there, it is just that R is looking for a cfa() function somewhere other than lavaan first, and using the first one that it finds.

  The foo::bar idiom is a form of defensive programming that always explicitly tells R where to look.  That way, the code will work no mater what you load in what order.

  If you do not like that idiom, you can avoid the problem by always listing lavaan last when you load your dependencies.  R will look for things from most recently loaded to least recently loaded.  However, this approach will not work if (a) you need two functions the names of which are shared between two packages and (b) you need one from each pair from each of the two packages.  That does not happen very often, but if it does you will need to use the explicit idiom or, alternatively, detach packages not currently being used.

Keith

http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
